reviews.title: Frustrating app and support experience
reviews.text:
I really wanted to like this app after seeing so many ads for it, but it ended up creating more work instead of making editing easier.

The AI edits were extremely overdone, so I switched to manual editing. Even then, the captions were noticeably out of sync with the audio and parts of the transcription were missing.

Support made the experience even more frustrating. I explained that I simply wanted a refund, but they continued trying to troubleshoot and told me their transcription model was one of the best available. They repeatedly asked me to send my original video through an iCloud link, but then accessed my existing project themselves and told me everything was working correctly on their end. It felt like my experience was being dismissed rather than acknowledged.

They eventually told me they canceled my subscription and issued a refund, which I have not received yet, so we’ll see.

For an app centered around captions and marketed as making video editing easier, I expected a much better experience.

reviews.title: Questionable Subscription Practices - Beware
reviews.text:
This subscription practice is extremely disappointing. In my experience, if you cancel your subscription, they take away the unused credits you already paid for instead of allowing you to use them through the end of your paid billing period.

Most subscription services allow you to cancel renewal while keeping access to what you paid for until the subscription period expires. At the very least, I would expect purchased credits to remain available until the end of that billing cycle. Here, it appears you have to keep the subscription active just to avoid losing your remaining credits.

That creates an unnecessary incentive to delay cancellation, which also makes it easier to forget and get charged again the following month.

If I paid for the month and received credits as part of that purchase, those credits should not simply disappear because I decided not to renew.

So here is the feedback this policy earned. I hope other customers are aware of how cancellation affects their unused credits before subscribing.

reviews.text:
I subscribed to the ‘Max’ package this week. Super excited. I uploaded my voice several times for my Ai twin and sounded nothing like me. I even tried added a clip of my voice which I’m happy with from eleven labs. And it wasn’t excepted? 
I loved everything else about the app. My Ai twin looked great. I love the captions. However…
All the credits of my ‘Max’ subscription was used up on trying to upload my voice. The voice sounded nothing like me and the voice upload feature would not except my external voice recording (made on eleven labs) 
Then I was told all my credits have been used. 
Im disappointed that I’m now not able to get on with my work…..
I Reached out to customer services and my option were 1. Wait till my next credits renew (a month away) or upgrade my subscription to ‘scale’. I feel using credits whilst familiarising myself and features not delivering as advertised is unreasonable.
customer services told me they cannot give me any credits back. ‘The system doesn’t allow this’. I have cancelled my subscription and put a claim into App Store under the basis the app does not work as advertised. My closing comments here is it’s ironic that I was given a ‘computer says no’ answer from a company that claims to be a Ai pioneer. Which resulted in me canceling my subscription. Stay clear of this app, unless you’re prepared to subscribe to the ‘scale x3 package £299 per month’ they have over promised on their ads and will not help you if you reach out. Daylight robbery.

reviews.title: Not worth paying for.
reviews.text: Before I do a formal review on the App Store, I would like to describe my experience using Captions. First and foremost, I want to clarify that this was a paid subscription.  The biggest issue that I had using this app was how the credits that were given to me were applied to correct AI inaccuracies.  There are many times when I use the descriptive AI function where I’d give a specific command and then AI would execute the command and when the edits were applied, they were significantly different than what I’d described. So in essence, a lot of my credits were not primarily used on editing. They were used to correct the inaccuracies that AI had applied to my projects. I also did not like the experience as a new user because it does take time to understand the app, and to understand how the edits look when you’re creating content. So when content was being created, and I was being charged for each edit, I didn’t like the fact that when I did not like the edit, I still had to pay for that using my own credit. I think that the app should give people an experimental time where we get familiar with all of the functions and then at some point, we begin being charged for the AI credits and things that we do. But the AI prompt section where we are to give descriptive information to me was a little fraudulent.  And that is the reason why I am canceling this app and canceling my paid subscription

reviews.title: Worst app ever
reviews.text:
Captions is honestly one of the worst apps I’ve tried. The moment you open it, you’re hit with nonstop pop-up ads and painfully cringey video intros that feel more like a marketing funnel than an actual editing tool.

The biggest issue is the pricing model. Instead of letting users actually test the features, the app immediately pushes you to buy a subscription. There’s barely any opportunity to try the tools before being forced into a paywall. For an app claiming to be AI-powered, that’s a terrible first impression.

Good apps let you explore features and then decide if they’re worth paying for. This one does the opposite. It feels like pure clickbait.

The AI chat feature is also broken or unreliable, which is ironic considering that’s one of the main things they promote.

Another red flag is how easy it is to delete the app. Most apps at least try to understand why users are leaving or offer feedback options. This one just lets you go instantly, which makes it feel like they know people will uninstall after seeing the paywall.

There are far better options out there. Apps like CapCut actually let you try features before asking you to pay, which is how it should be.

Overall: aggressive ads, forced subscriptions, buggy AI, and a bad user experience.

1/5 stars. Would not recommend.

Humanity managed to invent AI that can write symphonies and simulate galaxies, yet half the apps in the App Store still open like a late-night infomercial. Progress is a weird creature.

reviews.title: Best CAPS app ever!
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with my experience using your platform.

When I first started using the app, it was helpful. However, over time it has become clear that the credit system is designed in a way that burns through credits far faster than expected. The amount of credits promised versus how quickly they disappear does not feel transparent or fair.

On top of that, the app is now glitching in a way that directly affects my work and my money. I create content in Spanish. The platform is now automatically translating my scripts into English without my permission. This was not happening before. I can create one video successfully in Spanish, and seconds later, the next generation switches languages on its own.

When credits are consumed per generation, glitches are not a minor inconvenience — they cost real money.

Even more concerning: your advertised help desk and AI support are completely unresponsive. I reached out and received no assistance. No guidance. No clarification. Nothing.

At this point, the combination of:
   •   Rapid credit depletion
   •   Uncontrolled language auto-translation
   •   System instability between generations
   •   And zero meaningful customer support

makes this platform feel unreliable and financially wasteful.

Spanish creators should not be penalized by forced language switching. If the platform no longer properly supports Spanish content, that should be clearly disclosed.

I would strongly caution others to explore alternative tools un

This is such a painful experience, that I’ve started looking for other solutions that don’t eat my work, waste hours and ruin the project flow. Unfortunately need to keep using it for another week or so, but if you’re checking this out, don’t believe the hype of the ads you’ve seen. reviews.title: Single AI Test Forced an Upgrade and Blocked My Video
reviews.text:
I was a longtime subscriber and paid for the plan that included AI features. I spent a month editing a video, and at some point I tested one AI tool on a single photo. I didn’t keep the AI result, I removed it immediately and continued editing manually.

However, even though the AI output wasn’t used in the final project, Captions automatically stamped the entire project as an “AI used” file. When the app updated its tiers, my project suddenly required the new “Max” plan to download, even though my original subscription already included AI access. Support told me I was supposed to be grandfathered in, but I still cannot download my own video because of that single test on one picture.

I was told I would have to delete my entire project and start over. That’s extremely frustrating because the app encourages users to try AI tools, yet trying them even once permanently locks your project behind a higher tier. This wasn’t described anywhere, and it completely changed the value of the subscription I paid for.

I genuinely liked Captions and would love to return in the future, but constant tier changes during active memberships make it very hard to trust the system. I hope the team removes the permanent AI lock or offers a way for subscribers to recover their projects without being forced into an upgrade.

reviews.title: Beware: CaptionIO’s feature locked my work behind an upgrade paywall
reviews.text:
I subscribed to CaptionsIO  Pro, which clearly states that my plan includes AI usage and encourages users to “try AI features” as part of the subscription. I tried one of the AI tools, didn’t like the result, immediately undid it, and continued editing manually. 

However, the moment I tested the AI feature, CaptionIO permanently stamped my project as an “AI-used project”. Now I’m blocked from downloading my own video unless I upgrade again, even though I already pay for a Pro plan that supposedly includes AI features. 

This means that even if the AI output is undone - and even if the tool is used for a split second - the project becomes locked behind a higher tier. That is not clear upfront, and it goes against the impression that process subscribers can “try AI features” freely. It also penalizes users for experimenting with tools that are advertised as part of their paid plan.

I now have a finished project that I either have to redo completely or pay an additional upgrade for. This is extremely frustrating, feels misleading, and makes the “Pro” plan far less valuable than advertised. 

I hope captionIO clarifies these limitations and removes the permanent lock for users to simply test AI features that the Pro plan claims to include.
